items.title: GPT 6 is being pitched on knowledge per dollar instead of benchmark scores, and that one change tells you more than any
items.summary:
GPT 6 is being pitched on knowledge per dollar instead of benchmark scores, and that one change tells you more than any leaked capability list!

benchmark scores → capability claims → autonomy duration → cost per unit of knowledge

Benchmarks measure what a model does once, under ideal conditions, with a human watching.

Knowledge per dollar measures what it produces per unit of spend across long unsupervised runs.

Those two numbers stop agreeing the moment a model runs for hours instead of turns.

A model that is 5% worse and 70% cheaper wins every workload you run continuously.

The frame changed because the buyer changed, from researchers picking a winner to operators picking a cost curve.

Watch which number Sam Altman leads with in Washington. 

It tells you who he thinks is paying.

Everyone is still arguing about which model is smartest.

The people running agents all day stopped caring about that a while ago.

Follow @neil_xbt for more!

items.title: C'est carrément flippant.
items.summary:
C'est carrément flippant.

Quelqu'un a lancé GPT-5.6 Sol et Claude Fable 5 côte à côte.

Même prompt. Même tâche. Une seule tentative chacun.

Les deux ont réussi du premier coup.

La seule différence : Sol a terminé plus rapidement.

Personne ne s'y attendait.

Fable 5 était censé dominer les tâches de raisonnement complexe, sans véritable concurrence.

Vous avez moins de 24 heures pour mettre ça en place, car cela permet de récupérer 20 % de votre quota d'utilisation.

Enregistrez ce post et ajoutez-le à vos favoris, quoi qu'il arrive.

items.title: Employees at the world's biggest AI companies are calling ...
items.summary:
The letter comes on the heels of major advancements and burgeoning threats from rapidly developing AI systems. OpenAI disclosed last week that two of its test models escaped a lab environment, bypassed its systems to gain access to the open internet and hacked a different company’s internal system. [...] “We’re glad to see broad agreement across the field on the need for technical and governance tools to pace the frontier of AI development, including the ability to slow it, so society can prepare,” Anthropic said in a comment to CNN.

Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis also recently called for a new international standards body to help set protocols for new AI models, an idea endorsed by Altman, SpaceX’s Elon Musk, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and other major industry figures. [...] OpenAI said in a statement to CNN they agree with potentially pacing the development of AI, adding they “hope to contribute to work led by the U.S. government, alongside other labs” on the topic.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested it may be time to slow down AI development in a podcast interview Tuesday. The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress.

items.title: House Panel Weighs AI Job Gains Against Worker Risks
items.summary:
In April 2025, President Trump signed an executive order creating a White House task force on AI education and directing the Secretary of Labor to expand AI-related Registered Apprenticeships. The administration's AI Action Plan directs the Department of Labor to prioritize AI skill development across workforce funding streams and proposes an AI Workforce Research Hub. Beginning July 1, students became eligible for Pell Grants covering short-term programs in high-skill, in-demand fields. [...] ## The Bottom Line

Eight hearings in, the committee has built a case for AI as an opportunity engine without producing legislation that reconciles it with what Barlow and McBath described. Augusta made the tension concrete: the same technology anchoring a biomanufacturing plant and a new medical AI department also requires transmission lines running through civilians' properties.

Access the Legis1 platform for comprehensive political news, data, and insights. [...] ## What's Next

Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) introduced the AI Workforce Training Act in February, creating a 30 percent tax credit for employer-provided AI training. Sen. Jim Banks (R-IN) introduced the AI Workforce PREPARE Act in December 2025, which would establish an Artificial Intelligence Workforce Research Hub at the Department of Labor and require employers to disclose when AI was a substantial factor in a mass layoff. Both remain in committee.

items.title: Man sues OpenAI over ‘dangerous’ medical advice from ChatGPT
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO — A Florida man who sought health guidance on ChatGPT sued OpenAI Wednesday, claiming the artificial intelligence chatbot gave him dangerously inaccurate medical advice that led him to delay seeking professional treatment for a pulmonary embolism. [...] And Winters wants the court to pause the operation of ChatGPT Health, which OpenAI announced in January as a “a dedicated experience in ChatGPT designed for health and wellness,” unless “independent third parties determine the product to be safe through comprehensive safety audits."

“OpenAI cannot continue to treat human welfare as expendable in pursuit of market dominance,” Winters says in the complaint. [...] Winters accuses OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, of prioritizing profit over necessary guardrails and failing to warn users about critical safety concerns of ChatGPT-4o to secure a competitive advantage over other competitors in the AI industry.

items.title: Its AI agent spent days hacking a company, but sources say OpenAI ...
items.summary:
Four people familiar with OpenAI’s model-training practices say the company often runs several different model ​evaluations at the same time, all of which operate at high speeds and generate such enormous amounts of data that employees sometimes struggle to keep up.

By the time ​OpenAI alerted Hugging Face, the ⁠AI library had already called the FBI to report the hack, according to a person familiar with the matter. Reuters could not establish whether the bureau had opened an investigation. [...] The FBI declined to comment about the incident.

The incident, which evoked science fiction scenarios about humans losing control of dangerous AI systems, comes at a delicate ​time for OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT. Its executives are preparing for a possible initial public offering that could come as soon as this year to help finance the billions needed to fund its growth in years to come.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary:
OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place. [...] # What happened?

On July 16, Hugging Face said it had been hit by an unusually automated cyberattack. Over the course of a weekend, AI agents carried out thousands of actions across many temporary virtual computers, moving through the company’s internal systems and shifting the infrastructure coordinating the attack between online services to keep it running. Five days later, OpenAI disclosed that its own models were responsible.

items.title: How are companies, governments responding to the OpenAI hack?
items.summary:
ChatGPT owner OpenAI has admitted an “unprecedented cyber incident” – two of its most capable artificial intelligence models hacked into another AI company on their own – stirring debates over the need for stronger technology guardrails.

The company said its AI systems broke out of a testing environment and hacked startup Hugging Face.

The startup had disclosed on July 16 that its servers were hacked by an unknown but sophisticated agent acting on its own.
